source: console, 2026-10-17: `evolve clihealth usage agy` after wave 122; the operator approved a true share
title: The deep tier puts Argon first, so it spends all of Argon's weekly allowance in about four waves; share deep seats between Argon and Claude by budget
summary: Since #924 (2026-10-17) `cli_routing.tiers.deep` is [agy, agy-claude, claude], and the agy deep seat runs Gemini 4 Argon (Medium). The operator asked to share the Opus deep phase with Argon. A first-in-chain rule is not a share: every deep dispatch went to Argon until its group was exhausted. On 2026-10-17 at 22:15 (Asia/Taipei) `evolve clihealth usage agy` showed Gemini 4 Argon week 100% (reset in 153h 55m) and CLAUDE AND GPT MODELS week 100% (reset in 61h 56m), with GEMINI MODELS week at 42%. So every deep seat now falls through to Claude Code, which is at 67% of its week. Argon gives no deep capacity for about 6 days, and Claude carries the whole deep load.
fix: Make the deep tier share seats by budget, not by order. Research first, with a live web search: weighted and budget-paced routing (for example, token-bucket pacing, smooth weighted round-robin, and spend pacing as used in ad delivery). Write a design through skills/docs-write that compares at least 3 approaches, for example a fixed share per tier in cli_routing, a pace computed from each group's weekly used percent and its reset time, and a share that the advisor sets per phase. The router stays deterministic: the share is data in .evolve/policy.json cli_routing (written by `evolve cli-routing set`), and the pace input is the usage the bridge already reads (`evolve clihealth usage`). Keep the existing walk: an exhausted or benched target still falls through. No feature flag: the share is the routing table's own data.
acceptance: A design set (research, plan, ADR, spec) under docs/ compares at least 3 approaches and cites live sources; ste-lint --strict reports 0 findings.
With Argon at 0% used and 7 days to reset, a deep-tier walk over 100 simulated dispatches sends Argon about the configured share, not 100 (a unit test with an injected usage reader).
When the Argon group is paced to its budget, the next deep dispatch goes to the next healthy family in the chain, and `evolve cli-routing explain <agent>` prints the share and the pace.
An exhausted Argon group still benches only the Argon target (the cycle 1911 behavior is unchanged).
